title: Semantic addressing over opaque persistent state
question: Can a router identify a semantically relevant persistent state item when its address is opaque and absent from the public query?
hypothesis: H_address: explicit semantic state content is sufficient for a learned addressor to recover the relevant state item above the frozen no-learning control after a causal write/read boundary.

arms.name: analytic
arms.intervention: identity embeddings as an exact representability witness

arms.name: no_learning
arms.intervention: identical architecture with frozen random parameters

arms.name: shuffle
arms.intervention: preserve opaque addresses while swapping stored values

arms.name: reset
arms.intervention: clear all state after the causal write and before routing

endpoints.name: state_top1_recall
endpoints.role: primary — whether the correct opaque state address is selected
endpoints.description: Top-1 recall over the held-out state pool.

endpoints.name: end_to_end_top1_recall
endpoints.role: secondary — whether the retrieved semantic state resolves the exact downstream program choice

endpoints.name: mean_target_state_rank
endpoints.role: secondary — rank of the correct opaque state item

endpoints.name: inspected_state_items
endpoints.role: audit — state population inspected per decision

endpoints.name: reset_fail_closed
endpoints.role: audit — cleared state must not be silently replaced

decision_rule.condition: learned state_top1_recall exceeds no_learning state_top1_recall across the registered seeds and the endpoint is directionally above chance
decision_rule.licenses: bounded support for learned semantic addressing on the registered synthetic state pool
decision_rule.does_not_license: sublinear addressing, long-horizon memory, or general semantic retrieval

decision_rule.condition: learned state_top1_recall does not exceed no_learning state_top1_recall
decision_rule.licenses: the registered learner does not demonstrate exploitation of the semantic state signal
decision_rule.does_not_license: a claim that semantic addressing is impossible

held_constant: h_levels=8 denotes the persistent state-pool population in this experiment; the candidate program population is also fixed at 8
state write occurs one boundary before the read
state addresses are opaque randomized keys and never appear in the public query
exact downstream program matching is held fixed so the primary endpoint isolates state addressing
learning uses only verified selection success and the strongest in-pool negative
no epsilon-greedy or other exploration intervention is used
prior C5 and REP-001 through REP-005 evidence remains frozen
